rows.definition: issuecontract.WitnessedEnvelope (JSON witnessed_operating_envelope) is the string field on a project-work item / issue contract / handoff carrying the currently-witnessed operating envelope - the observed baseline, target, and completion-standard envelope an operator has directly verified, distinct from the TargetEnvelope that is merely declared.
rows.distinction: The OBSERVED operating-envelope section on an issue contract, not a world-state witness (a cache-coherence binding in vdso) and not a WitnessOutcome (a gate verdict). It witnesses an ISSUE'S scope, not a cache entry or a claim.

rows.definition: modelroute.CrossAuditRefute (CrossAuditVerdict = REFUTE) is the cross-audit verdict meaning a model-route quality audit found evidence that CONTRADICTS a model's claimed routing behavior, alongside CrossAuditPass / CrossAuditInconclusive / CrossAuditUnavailable.
rows.distinction: A cross-audit verdict about MODEL-ROUTE quality, not the cache-coherence Refutation (a local invalidation of a world-state witness) and not abi.WitnessRefuted (a gate-level outcome). Three refusals in three subsystems sharing the refute root.

rows.definition: resume.ContinuityWitness is the per-resume verified-progress verdict: a fold of trajctl W3 ScoreRows across the launch boundary that reports whether the objective's witnessed curve actually advanced (Witnessed + Advanced), or whether the resume only produced turns without moving verified progress.
rows.distinction: A per-RESUME progress fold over trajctl W3 rows, not a world-state witness (a cache-coherence binding) and not a WitnessOutcome (a single gate verdict). It witnesses resume PROGRESS, not a cache entry or a claim corroboration.

rows.definition: cmd/fak.emitTrunkRedWitness records one pre-existing-red admission to the shared trunk-red ledger (FAIL-OPEN: a no-op when recording is disabled or no failing package was parsed), folding the ledger to return occurrence and session counts so the caller can print an honest convergence line.
rows.distinction: The RECORDER function that appends a trunk-red witness row to the shared ledger, not buildwitness (a structural compile guard) and not worktreewitness (a detached-trunk command harness). Each witnesses a different kind of build fact.

rows.definition: cmd/fak.trunkRedWitnessNote renders the convergence line appended to a gate's pre-existing-red advisory ONLY when the row was actually written, making the shared-break payoff visible (how many clones are stuck on this break across how many sessions).
rows.distinction: The RENDERER of the human-readable convergence note, not emitTrunkRedWitness (the recorder that writes the ledger row it reads from). One writes the witness; the other renders its payoff.

rows.definition: loopmgr.Policy.MinWitnessRate (float64, JSON min_witness_rate) is the governor policy floor: a loop whose witnessed/claimed completion ratio drops below this rate is refused new admissions, because its runs are predominantly self-reported rather than independently confirmed.
rows.distinction: The POLICY FLOOR (a configured threshold), not ReasonWitnessCollapse (the refuse reason the governor emits when below it) and not WitnessCollapse (the health descriptor that reports the majority-unwitnessed state). Threshold vs reason vs descriptor.

rows.definition: loopmgr.ReasonWitnessCollapse (const WITNESS_COLLAPSE) is the structured refuse reason the loop governor emits when it denies admission to a loop whose witnessed/claimed completion ratio fell below Policy.MinWitnessRate.
rows.distinction: The REFUSE REASON constant the governor cites, not MinWitnessRate (the policy floor it enforces) and not WitnessCollapse (the health descriptor that reports the state without refusing). A reason code vs a threshold vs a descriptor.

rows.definition: loopmgr.WitnessCollapse (bool on HealthRow, int on HealthRollup) is the advisory health descriptor: true on a per-loop row when a MAJORITY of ended runs went unwitnessed (Witnessed*2 < Runs), and the fleet-wide count of such loops on the rollup. It is descriptive, not a gate.
rows.distinction: The HEALTH DESCRIPTOR that reports majority-unwitnessed state for the pane, not ReasonWitnessCollapse (the governor refuse reason) and not MinWitnessRate (the policy floor). It describes the symptom; the governor acts on the threshold.

rows.definition: modelscore.ReconstructionWitness (JSON reconstruction_witness) is the provenance string on a model-score record naming how the model was reconstructed (e.g. committed benchmark snapshot), required for the reconstructed-from-blog provenance tier alongside submission_source and author_source.
rows.distinction: A PROVENANCE string on a model-score record naming the reconstruction method, not a world-state witness (a cache-coherence binding) and not ProvenanceWitnessed (an evidence-strength label on a context-envelope). It witnesses a MODEL'S ORIGIN, not a cache entry or a context row.

rows.definition: issuecontract.StrictWitness (bool, JSON strict_witness, CLI --strict-witness) is the flag that promotes any non-strong WitnessGrade to a hold: when true, an issue whose done-condition witness is weak, forgeable, or missing is held for triage instead of dispatched.
rows.distinction: The POLICY FLAG that escalates non-strong grades to holds, not WitnessGrade (the readout it gates) and not WitnessGradeStrong (the grade value it checks against). A gate on a grade vs the grade itself vs its strongest value.

rows.definition: issuecontract.WitnessGrade is the advisory-first pre-dispatch forgeability readout for a ticket's done condition: it grades the witness as strong (independent oracle named), weak (no oracle), forgeable (self-claim only), or missing (no witness declared), carrying flags and evidence.
rows.distinction: The pre-dispatch FORGEABILITY READOUT on an issue contract, not a WitnessOutcome (a gate-level corroboration verdict) and not the WitnessResolver (the engine that corroborates). It grades an ISSUE'S witness before dispatch, not a claim at adjudication.

rows.definition: issuecontract.WitnessGradeStrong (const strong) is the strongest of four WitnessGrade values, meaning the done-condition witness names an independent oracle (go test, make ci, fak, dos, git show, a fixture, a render, an exit code, a ledger, etc.) that can corroborate the claimed effect.
rows.distinction: One VALUE of the WitnessGrade enum (the strongest), not WitnessGrade (the readout struct that holds it) and not WitnessConfirmed (a gate-level outcome). A grade value vs the grade readout vs a corroboration outcome.

rows.definition: deletioncert.WitnessName (JSON witness_name) is the string field on a deletion certificate naming the vDSO world-state witness under which the evicted entries were admitted (empty if none), pinning the eviction receipt to the integrity epoch it occurred under.
rows.distinction: The NAME FIELD on a deletion certificate carrying a world-state witness identifier, not the world-state witness value itself and not the WitnessResolver (the engine that corroborates claims). A reference to a witness vs the witness vs the resolver.

rows.definition: WitnessDir is the on-disk directory constant where witness artifacts are stored, declared independently in multiple packages: mlpscore.WitnessDir (docs/mlp/witnesses) for MLP witness manifests, qwen36parity.WitnessDir (experiments/agent-live) for Mac parity witnesses, and benchloop fleet dispatch's witnessDir for bench-fleet witness JSON.
rows.distinction: A FILESYSTEM PATH convention for storing witness artifacts on disk, not a world-state witness (a cache-coherence binding) and not the WitnessResolver (an engine that corroborates claims). Where witnesses are STORED vs what they BIND vs what RESOLVES them.
